headline: Benchmarks of learned models for biological sequence, connectome, and perturbation data
label: Scalable Genomic Sequence Models
summary: Pretrained embeddings, alignment-free classifiers and transformers are being benchmarked against alternative methods across genomic and single-cell tasks.
synthesis: The items share a comparative-evaluation emphasis on learned models for biological data, though they differ in data type and task. A benchmark of four GNNs against four non-graph methods classifies C. elegans neurons from functional connectome features. Another benchmark covers over 600 embedding-task pairs to test whether pretrained embeddings, including biological foundation models, improve single-cell perturbation response prediction. DiCNN-UniK, a dual-input CNN over unique k-mer embeddings, classifies flavivirus genomes without alignment and reaches 99% accuracy on partial genomes down to 20%. BarcodeBERT applies transformers to DNA barcodes for biodiversity analyses. The dominant thread is systematic assessment of whether architecture or input representation changes outcomes, with reduced input explicit only for DiCNN-UniK. What is new is the attention to graph structure, pretrained embeddings, and alignment-free k-mer representations as alternatives to established approaches.
